name: backend_s3
description: Terraform S3 backend configuration for remote state storage. Stores the Terraform state file in an S3 bucket with optional state locking via DynamoDB. This is the recommended backend for production AWS deployments as it provides versioning, encryption, locking, and team collaboration.
use_cases: State versioning and recovery from corruption
State locking to prevent concurrent modifications

required.name: bucket
required.description: The name of the S3 bucket to store state. Must be globally unique. Must exist before terraform init.

required.name: key
required.description: The path to the state file inside the S3 bucket. Convention: '{project}/{environment}/terraform.tfstate'

required.name: region
required.description: The AWS region where the S3 bucket is located.

optional.name: dynamodb_table
optional.description: DynamoDB table name for state locking. Table must have a primary key named 'LockID' of type String.

optional.name: encrypt
optional.description: Enable server-side encryption of the state file. Defaults to false. Strongly recommended: true.

optional.name: kms_key_id
optional.description: KMS key ARN or alias for SSE-KMS encryption. If omitted with encrypt=true, uses SSE-S3.

optional.name: role_arn
optional.description: IAM role ARN to assume before accessing the S3 bucket.

best_practices: Always enable encryption (encrypt = true) and versioning on the S3 bucket
Use DynamoDB table for state locking to prevent concurrent apply operations
Block all public access on the S3 bucket — state files can contain sensitive data
Use a separate AWS account or at minimum a separate S3 bucket per environment
Use KMS with customer-managed keys for compliance requirements
Enable S3 bucket versioning for state recovery from corruption
Use IAM policies to restrict who can read/write the state bucket
security_notes: Terraform state files can contain sensitive data (passwords, private keys) — always encrypt
Apply bucket policies to deny unencrypted uploads
Enable S3 access logging on the state bucket for compliance
Use IAM role assumption (role_arn) instead of long-term credentials for CI/CD
Never commit terraform.tfstate files to version control

common_errors.error: Backend initialization failed: S3 bucket not found
common_errors.fix: Create the S3 bucket BEFORE running terraform init with the S3 backend. Run with local backend first, then migrate

common_errors.error: Error locking state: table not found
common_errors.fix: Create the DynamoDB table with hash_key='LockID' (String type) before using dynamodb_table parameter

common_errors.error: Variables not allowed in backend configuration
common_errors.fix: Backend configuration cannot use Terraform variables. Use partial configuration with -backend-config flag or hardcode values
